notes.title: Beta update: Camera Calibration tool
notes.notes:
Today's beta update (v. 0.14.0.6) features:

A Camera Calibration screen where you can align the left and right camera images with real world objects. 
For calibration you need two controllers. One controller functions as the object that you will align the camera image with. For best results, place this controller at the same distance from the headset as the objects you want to see in VR. E.g., if you use the app to see a racing wheel, button box, HOTAS or airplane instrument panel, then place the controller next to those objects during calibration.
You need to be able to see the controller's 3D model in VR. Don't use the SteamVR Home with the mountain house, but use the older SteamVR Home (the empty space with stars and a mountain ridge in the distance).
There's an instruction page you can reach from the Camera Calibration page.
To get to the Camera Calibration page, follow the link on the Camera Setup page.

If you're not on the Beta branch yet, go to your Steam library, right click the Reality Mixer app, choose Properties, click the BETAS tab and choose the beta branch from the drop down list.

If you encounter any problems, please tell. You can always go back to the previous beta in the BETAS tab in your Steam Library.

notes.title: Beta update: Camera setup, WMR right camera use and initial chromakey support
notes.notes:
Today's beta update (v. 0.13.0.14) features:

A camera setup screen where you can choose to use left, right or both cameras. (Most of the work involved in this was necessary to support external USB cameras later on.)
Initial chromakey (greenscreen) support.

If you turn on both cameras, you'll notice (on WMR) the images aren't lined up well. Next update will bring a calibration tool. 
(On a Valve Index the left and right images already line up quite OK.)

If you encounter any problems, please tell. You can always go back to the previous beta in the BETAS tab in your Steam Library.

notes.title: v.0.12.0.6 beta - Update for HP G2 v1
notes.notes:
Edit:

The November 20 beta update has a Camera Setup page on the SteamVR Dashboard for Reality Mixer. There you can adjust the camera rotation while in VR.


Old text:

Here's a temporary fix for the rotated view on HP G2 v1 headsets.

[olist]
Update to the new beta (version 0.12.0.6).
Run the app once in SteamVR.
Quit SteamVR (or just the Reality Mixer app).
Find the .xml settings file in the install folder of Reality Mixer. It's named like RealityMixer_Settings_RoomId-[some number].xml.
Open it in Notepad.
Find the entry for parameter "LeftCameraRotationZ".
If you have a HP G2 v1, set it to "0".
Save the settings file.
Start SteamVR and the Reality Mixer app.
[/olist]
Please share your experience and let me know how well (or bad) the image lines up with the real world when using a G2 v1.

notes.title: Update v.0.10.2.11
notes.notes:
Reality Mixer has been updated with the following changes:


Activate a camera box using a button on your VR controller. Select a different, or the same, button for several camera boxes, the floor viewer, the lap viewer or cockpit. (This is in addition to the button activation using a keyboard or joystick button.)
Leash: When editing the camera boxes a 'leash', or line, is shown from the Box Edit Panel to the selected box. This makes it easier to find boxes and to see which one you're currently editing on the Edit Panel.
The Box Edit Panel does not fade out anymore when resizing or moving boxes. Instead, it will show a 'panel is disabled' screen.
You can now click anywhere on the background of the panel to move/drag it through the world.
Brightness and contrast sliders are a bit less sensitive.
User can turn on/off keyboard editing of boxes (for move/rotate/size).
A different method for calculating a RoomID is now used, preventing lots of settings .xml files on certain systems.

Tip: Use Voice Attack to show and hide boxes by speaking commands such as "Show keyboard", "Show HOTAS", "Show drinks", "Show couch", "Show desk", etc.
Configure Voice Attack to press the same keyboard button as you have configured with "Activate by button" in the Box Edit Panel.

All feedback welcome!

notes.title: Reality Mixer Update: New Activation Options, a Floor Viewer and a Lap Viewer
notes.notes:
This May 2022 update provides:

Activate by Gaze Angle: Look straight at a camera box to make it visible. Use this activation method with seated games where you have things on a table next to your seat. The activation angle and optional activation delay can be configured. Using an activation delay means you have to look at the object for a second before it starts to show itself, to prevent accidental activation.
Activate by Button Press: Press a keyboard, mouse, gamepad, HOTAS or racing wheel button to turn on/off a camera box.
Floor Viewer: To quickly see the real floor around your feet.
Lap Viewer: For use with seated experiences such as Big Screen. Lap Viewer can be used for quick glances at a normal (untracked) keyboard on your lap.
Slider for camera brightness adjustment.
Slider for camera contrast adjustment.
Toggle for using transparency instead of static (white noise) for areas the camera can't see.

Floor Viewer and Lap Viewer both use Gaze Angle Activation by default, but could use Proximity or ButtonPress activation as well.

If you have any questions, remarks or ideas, please share.

notes.title: Reality Mixer Update - Attach to Tracked Devices, Modify Box Edges and more
notes.notes:
Reality Mixer has been updated with the following changes:

Attach to tracked devices: A camera box can be anchored to a tracked device such as a controller, headset or Vive or Tundra tracker. If the tracked device is attached to e.g. a (real) wireless keyboard, you can move the keyboard through your play area and see it when you look at it. Attach a tracker to a swivel chair with wheels and take the chair with you in VR.
Edit box edges: Reduce brightness of the sparkling edges or turn off the edges completely. Increase width of the edges, which is also used for smooth fade-ins when using a Cockpit Box.
Min/max transparency of boxes: If you set the maximum opacity of a box to e.g. 50%, you'll see the VR world pass through the camera box or cockpit, increasing the feeling of reality. Great for Simracing and Flightsim experiences using racing wheels or HOTAS.
Move/drag Box Edit Panel: When editing camera boxes, you can now position the panel yourself by dragging it. Use the icon in the top left corner to move the panel.

If you have any questions or comments, please let me know.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41647813/a9388ed4b7a3be8d2499b8a8e23d2bc3e78658e4.png
